Characteristic 'trefoil with a single fruit' sign, with relative sparing of the gracilis, sartorius, adductor longus, and semitendinosus.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real axial T1-WI and T2 DIXON muscle MRI of a DMD patient (N3) at age 7, showing the characteristic thigh involvement pattern with fatty infiltration of adductor magnus/biceps femoris, severe gluteal fatty replacement, and relative gracilis/sartorius sparing — a textbook DMD MRI presentation in a child. B: Real axial T1-WI and T2 DIXON muscle MRI of the same DMD patient (N3) at age 8, demonstrating progressive fatty infiltration of the quadriceps and persistent severe gluteal involvement — a classic DMD MRI manifestation in a child, directly comparable to panel A.

International journal of molecular sciences 2025. doi:10.3390/ijms26199389. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Muscle MRI of patient N3 at age 7 (A) and 8 (B). Consecutive axial T1-weighted MRI images of the thighs demonstrate a characteristic “trefoil with a single fruit” sign, with severe involvement of the adductor magnus and biceps femoris and relative sparing of the gracilis, sartorius, adductor longus, and semitendinosus. A comparison of the two time points reveals disease progression, evidenced by increased fatty infiltration within the quadriceps muscles over the one-year interval. All gluteal muscle subgroups (maximus, medius, minimus) were severely affected by fatty replacement. In the distal lower limbs, the peroneus longus and medial gastrocnemius muscles showed moderate fatty infiltration.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Quantitative T2 maps of the lower leg and thigh from the Duchenne muscular dystrophy cohort show myopathic muscle T2 heterogeneity/edema-like signal, but the controlled vocabulary has no T2-specific finding, so the visible abnormality is recorded as a proposed finding. B: Human T1-weighted MRI of calf and thigh with spectroscopy voxels placed in soleus and vastus lateralis for fat-fraction quantification; intramuscular fat replacement is visible and fits the DMD proximal muscle fatty-replacement MRI pattern. C: Representative DMD participant in the fastest functional group; T1-weighted calf and thigh images with matched spectra show only mild soleus/vastus lateralis fat fraction, visually consistent with early DMD fatty replacement. D: Human DMD MRI/MRS example in an intermediate functional group shows visibly increased soleus and vastus lateralis fat infiltration on T1-weighted images, with spectra quantifying higher fat...
panels.attribution_text: Barnard et al. Skeletal muscle magnetic resonance biomarkers correlate with function and sentinel events in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.. PloS one 2018. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0194283. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Representative T2 maps, 1H MRS voxel placement, and 1H MR spectra. A) T2 maps were created from the 40, 60, 80, and 100ms TE spin echo images of the lower leg and thigh. Utilizing the popliteus and biceps femoris short head as standardized anatomical landmarks to guide lower leg and thigh slice selection, the TA, PER, TP, SOL, MG, VL, BFLH, and GRA muscles were traced on three contiguous slices to determine mean T2 for each muscle. B) T1-weighted images demonstrate the location of voxel placement for MR spectroscopy used to quantify FF. Voxels were sized as large as possible while staying completely within the SOL and VL muscles, avoiding the fascia. The voxel position from prior years was referenced to position voxels at an anatomically similar location at follow-up visits.
